Africa.name: Lion
Africa.description: I am Leo the Lion! I live in sunny grasslands.
Africa.funFact: Lions live in groups called prides!

Africa.name: African Elephant
Africa.description: I am an African Elephant, the largest land animal.
Africa.funFact: An elephant's trunk has over 40,000 muscles!

Africa.name: Giraffe
Africa.description: I am a tall Giraffe! I love eating leaves from the treetops.
Africa.funFact: Giraffes have the same number of neck vertebrae as humans—just much bigger!

Africa.name: Zebra
Africa.description: I am a Zebra with cool black and white stripes.
Africa.funFact: No two zebras have the same stripe pattern.

Africa.name: Hippopotamus
Africa.description: I am a Hippo! I love spending time in the water.
Africa.funFact: Hippos secrete a reddish substance that acts as a natural sunscreen.

Asia.name: Giant Panda
Asia.description: I am a Giant Panda! I eat a lot of bamboo.
Asia.funFact: Pandas can eat up to 38 kilos of bamboo every day!

Asia.name: Bengal Tiger
Asia.description: I am a Bengal Tiger! I am a very strong swimmer.
Asia.funFact: A tiger's roar can be heard as far as 3 kilometers away!

Asia.name: Orangutan
Asia.description: I am an Orangutan. I spend most of my time in trees.
Asia.funFact: Orangutans are the heaviest tree-dwelling animals.

Asia.name: Snow Leopard
Asia.description: I am a Snow Leopard! I live in high, snowy mountains.
Asia.funFact: Snow leopards have long tails they use like blankets to keep warm!

Asia.name: Bactrian Camel
Asia.description: I am a Bactrian Camel. I have two humps!
Asia.funFact: A camel's humps store fat, not water, which gives them energy.

North America.name: Bald Eagle
North America.description: I am a Bald Eagle! I can fly very high and have great eyesight.
North America.funFact: Bald eagles can spot a fish from a mile away!

North America.name: Grizzly Bear
North America.description: I am a Grizzly Bear. I love catching salmon in the river.
North America.funFact: Grizzly bears hibernate for up to 7 months a year.

North America.name: Moose
North America.description: I am a Moose! I am the largest member of the deer family.
North America.funFact: A moose's antlers can spread over 6 feet wide!

North America.name: Gray Wolf
North America.description: I am a Gray Wolf. I travel with my family pack.
North America.funFact: Wolves howl to communicate with other members of their pack.

North America.name: Raccoon
North America.description: I am a Raccoon! I wear a natural mask and I am very curious.
North America.funFact: Raccoons have highly sensitive front paws that they use to 'see' their food.

South America.name: Jaguar
South America.description: I am a Jaguar! I live in the rainforest.
South America.funFact: Jaguars have the strongest bite of any big cat!

South America.name: Three-toed Sloth
South America.description: I am a Sloth. I move very slowly through the trees.
South America.funFact: Sloths move so slowly that algae actually grows on their fur.

South America.name: Toco Toucan
South America.description: I am a Toucan! Look at my colorful beak!
South America.funFact: A toucan's beak makes up about a third of its entire length!

South America.name: Llama
South America.description: I am a Llama. I live high up in the Andes mountains.
South America.funFact: Llamas are very social and live with other llamas as a herd.

South America.name: Capybara
South America.description: I am a Capybara. I'm the biggest rodent in the world.
South America.funFact: Capybaras are excellent swimmers and can hold their breath for 5 minutes.

Europe.name: Brown Bear
Europe.description: I am a Brown Bear! I live in European forests.
Europe.funFact: Brown bears can run very fast, up to 30 miles per hour!

Europe.name: Reindeer
Europe.description: I am a Reindeer! I live in the snowy north.
Europe.funFact: Both male and female reindeer grow antlers.

Europe.name: Red Fox
Europe.description: I am a Red Fox. I am very clever.
Europe.funFact: Foxes use the Earth's magnetic field to help them hunt.

Europe.name: Eurasian Lynx
Europe.description: I am a Lynx! I have tufts of hair on my ears.
Europe.funFact: A lynx's big furry paws act like natural snowshoes.

Australia.name: Kangaroo
Australia.description: I am a Kangaroo! I can jump really far.
Australia.funFact: Kangaroos use their strong tail for balance while hopping.

Australia.name: Koala
Australia.description: I am a Koala. I spend my days sleeping in eucalyptus trees.
Australia.funFact: Koalas can sleep up to 22 hours a day!

Australia.name: Platypus
Australia.description: I am a Platypus. I have a bill like a duck and I lay eggs.

Australia.name: Emu
Australia.description: I am an Emu! I am a bird but I cannot fly.
Australia.funFact: Emus are the second-tallest bird in the world, after the ostrich.

Australia.name: Tasmanian Devil
Australia.description: I am a Tasmanian Devil! I live on the island of Tasmania.
Australia.funFact: Tasmanian devils have one of the most powerful bites of any mammal for their size.

Antarctica.name: Emperor Penguin
Antarctica.description: I am a Penguin! I love sliding on the ice.
Antarctica.funFact: Emperor penguins huddle together to stay warm in the freezing cold.

Antarctica.name: Weddell Seal
Antarctica.description: I am a Seal! I am a great swimmer.
Antarctica.funFact: Weddell seals can hold their breath for up to 80 minutes underwater.

Antarctica.name: Walrus
Antarctica.description: I am a Walrus! I have long tusks.
Antarctica.funFact: Walruses can sleep while floating in the water!

Antarctica.name: Polar Bear
Antarctica.description: I am a Polar Bear! I live near the North Pole.
Antarctica.funFact: Polar bear fur is actually transparent, not white!
